item.content:encoded:
The New Ireland Police Command officially welcomed its new leader today during a handover-takeover ceremony at the Kavieng police headquarters, marking the transition of the Provincial Police Commander (PPC) post from Chief Superintendent Albert Beli to Chief Superintendent George Fanamanu.

Chief Superintendent Fanamanu, is a senior officer from the New Zealand Police originally from Tonga, recently took his oath of office in Port Moresby.

He becomes the eighth Commonwealth Police Officer to join the ranks of the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary (RPNGC) under ongoing international police partnership programs, bringing extensive Pacific region experience to his new role in New Ireland Province.

Addressing the officers during the ceremony, Chief Superintendent Beli expressed his gratitude to the local constabulary and the community for their support during his tenure.

Incoming PPC Fanamanu expressed his commitment to maintaining law and order, strengthening community relationships, and supporting local frontline officers throughout the province.

item.title: Police launch Highlands Western Strategic Plan for NATEL 2027
item.description: Acting Assistant Commissioner of Police Chief Superintendent, Joseph Tondop has announced a new Highlands Western Division Strategic Plan aimed at ensuring a free, fair and safe National Election in 2027. As Divisional Commander for the Highlands Western Division, covering Hela, Southern Highlands and Enga, Chief Supt Tondop said the plan was developed based on ground realities, police capacity an
item.content:encoded:
Acting Assistant Commissioner of Police Chief Superintendent, Joseph Tondop has announced a new Highlands Western Division Strategic Plan aimed at ensuring a free, fair and safe National Election in 2027.

As Divisional Commander for the Highlands Western Division, covering Hela, Southern Highlands and Enga, Chief Supt Tondop said the plan was developed based on ground realities, police capacity and threat assessments.

"This Strategic Plan covers two phases. Phase 1 will run in the third and fourth quarters of 2026, and Phase 2 in the first and second quarters of 2027," he said.

The plan focuses on three key objectives:

2. Protection of Critical Economic Corridors

3. Containment of Small arms and light weapons (SALW) Proliferation

The expected outcomes are: secured voting spaces, guaranteed voter access, SALW mitigation, accountability for actions, and restored public trust in institutions.

"This strategy is anchored on Section 50 of the Constitution - the right to vote. Every eligible voter must be able to cast their vote without fear or intimidation," Supt Tondop said.

After consultations with Provincial Police Commanders and Provincial Security Coordinators, police have adopted what the commander calls a "force-multiplier" approach.

This includes community mobilisation and an Amalgamated Polling Booth Option, where multiple polling points are consolidated to concentrate security and reduce risks.

Key pillars include public awareness, education, civil society engagement, student leadership involvement, NGO partnerships, intelligence gathering, control of transport routes, and enhanced police force deployment.

Chief Supt Tondop identified major risks as political interference, SALW and ammunition supply, budget delays, and armed confrontations.

He called on stakeholders to support implementation starting in Q3 2026.

These include extractive resource companies, major businesses, international partners, provincial governments, DDAs, and GoPNG for election funding. Support is also needed from every LLG and Council Ward.

"I am also appealing to all tertiary students from Hela, SHP and Enga studying across PNG. We will work with your provincial education boards. Help us educate your people so we can deliver NATEL 2027 safely," he said.

item.title: Simbu PHA Board concludes three-year term
item.description: Simbu Provincial Health Authority Chief Executive Officer, Dr. Ken Kassi formally commended the outgoing Board of Governance for its decisive leadership and support over the past three years. Speaking during the board’s farewell over the weekend, Dr. Kassi said the board’s guidance was instrumental in driving major improvements in healthcare delivery across the province.
item.content:encoded:
Simbu Provincial Health Authority Chief Executive Officer, Dr. Ken Kassi formally commended the outgoing Board of Governance for its decisive leadership and support over the past three years.

Speaking during the board’s farewell over the weekend, Dr. Kassi said the board’s guidance was instrumental in driving major improvements in healthcare delivery across the province.

"Your commitment, vision and partnership with management have positioned Simbu PHA as one of the top-performing health authorities in the country," Dr. Kassi said.

The outgoing board officially concluded its three-year tenure, leaving behind a legacy of performance excellence.

Their collaborative relationship with management was credited for Simbu PHA securing second place nationwide in the 2025 Sector Performance Annual Review, SPAR, report.

Cultivating a positive mindset and building strong partnerships were key themes highlighted during the farewell.

Outgoing Board Chairman David Herman Nime said positive thinking and teamwork are the tools to achieve greater results.

"When a mind is cultivated with negativity, it is just like you drinking poison and expecting someone else to die on your behalf," he said.

Mr. Nime said, despite members coming from non-medical backgrounds, their commitment to public service yielded tangible results for the community.

During this transition period, the CEO will assume all operational authority and will report directly to the National Minister for Health until a new board is appointed.

Management assures the public that health service operations across the province will continue without disruption during the interim period.

item.title: Hagen Show opens doors for new cultural groups and international visitors
item.description: The 66th Mt Hagen Culture and Agriculture Show has opened its doors to more than traditional performances. The three-day show at the weekend (14 th -16 th August) gave cultural groups and international visitors an opportunity to experience Papua New Guinea’s rich cultural diversity.
item.content:encoded:
The 66th Mt Hagen Culture and Agriculture Show has opened its doors to more than traditional performances.

The three-day show at the weekend (14 th -16 th August) gave cultural groups and international visitors an opportunity to experience Papua New Guinea’s rich cultural diversity.

Among those making their first appearance at the Hagen Show is a cultural group from Koinambe, an area bordering Jiwaka and Madang Provinces.

For the group, taking part in one of Papua New Guinea’s biggest cultural gatherings has been made possible through its involvement with Redfern Ecotourism Lodge.

The Koinambe Waire Brukim Kumul Group leader, Lucas Mondia says the opportunity is an important step in taking its culture beyond its home community and sharing it with a wider audience.

The participation also reflects the wider reach of this year’s show, which has brought together cultural groups, businesses, farmers, tourists and visitors at Queen’s Park in Mt Hagen.

Hagen Show Chairman, Pym Mamindi says the involvement of new groups is one of the things that makes the annual event important.

" On behalf of the Hagen Show committee I would sincerely like to thank those who were involved in this year's Show. If it wasn't for you guys the Show wouldn't have even happened at all.," Mamindi said.

He thanked the sponsors for coming on board and helping the committee stage the 66th Hagen Show, despite preparations being made at relatively short notice.

The Western Highlands Provincial Government also provided K500,000 in support of the event.

The Hagen Show Chairman adds the support has helped the committee bring together the different elements needed to host the show and provide an opportunity for cultural groups to participate.

But the impact of the show goes beyond the cultural groups.

For international visitor Bryan, from Philadelphia in the United States, this is his first visit to Papua New Guinea and his first Hagen Show.

He says the experience has given him a different view of Papua New Guinean culture and its people.

"I have always dreamed to come to PNG. While I was in Australia I realized that dream was possible. And so I planned it for almost six months and now I'm here and I have no idea what to expect and the experience of the Hagen Show is like no other I have experienced."

Bryan describes the people as warm and welcoming, saying he will return home with good memories and beautiful photographs from the Hagen Show.

"For 15 years I have been looking at PNG and Hagen Show on other people's social media posts and planned that I need to go there. And now that I'm here I can say the people are very warm and helpful and not only that but the culture here I've seen is deeper than any other places that I've seen and it's beautiful," says Bryan from Philadelphia.

For the Koinambe cultural group, and visitors like Bryan, the event is more than a three-day celebration.

It is a chance for communities to share their identity, for visitors to experience cultures they may never have seen before, and for the Hagen Show to continue expanding its role as a meeting place for people from Papua New Guinea and around the world.

And for Chairman Mamindi, the support received this year has helped make that possible.

He says the committee remains grateful to every sponsor and organisation that contributed to bringing the 66th Hagen Show to life.

item.title: NDC expects El Nino peak between September and October
item.description: Papua New Guinea is heading into the most critical months of the El Nino period, with the National Disaster Centre (NDC) preparing to assess whether provinces can cope with worsening conditions. The centre expects the peak between September and December.
item.content:encoded:
Papua New Guinea is heading into the most critical months of the El Nino period, with the National Disaster Centre (NDC) preparing to assess whether provinces can cope with worsening conditions.

The centre expects the peak between September and December.

Acting Director of Operations and Emergency Response, Andrew Oaego says inter-agency assessment teams will begin visiting affected provinces from the end of August.

The teams will check the impact of El Nino and whether provincial authorities have enough resources to respond.

Several provinces are already on alert or watch stages, with the NDC monitoring conditions.

Oaego says the assessments are important because the level of support needed will depend on how badly individual provinces are affected.

He says provinces are expected to use their own response plans and resources first.

The NDC steps in when a disaster becomes too large for a province to manage alone.

The assessment teams will work with provincial authorities and other agencies to identify gaps and areas that may need national support.

For communities, the next few months could be critical as authorities move from monitoring conditions to checking how prepared provinces are to respond.

The centre is urging provinces to keep their response plans active and continue monitoring conditions as the El Nino peak approaches.

item.title: Australia and PNG advance on Pukpuk Treaty
item.description: Australia’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Defence, Richard Marles, and Papua New Guinea’s Minister for Defence, Elias Kapavore MP, met on Sunday 16th August, in Port Moresby for their first ministerial meeting. During their discussions, Deputy Prime Minister Marles reaffirmed the close and enduring partnership between Australia and Papua New Guinea.
item.content:encoded:
Australia’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Defence, Richard Marles, and Papua New Guinea’s Minister for Defence, Elias Kapavore MP, met on Sunday 16th August, in Port Moresby for their first ministerial meeting.

During their discussions, Deputy Prime Minister Marles reaffirmed the close and enduring partnership between Australia and Papua New Guinea.

The Pukpuk Treaty – which entered into force on 8 July 2026 – is Papua New Guinea’s first alliance with any country, and Australia’s first in more than 70 years.

The ministers spoke about opportunities to further deepen defence ties and implement priority initiatives under the Pukpuk Treaty, including the development of a recruitment pathway to enable PNG citizens to join the Australian Defence Force (ADF).

Deputy Prime Minister Marles said Australia and Papua New Guinea are the closest of partners and friends, and now allies.

“With the Pukpuk Treaty now in force, we are focused on the next phase of our partnership and delivering practical outcomes that strengthen cooperation between our defence forces and advance our shared security interests.

"I look forward to working with Minister Kapavore to progress the Papua New Guinea recruitment pathway to the ADF, with a shared aspiration to have a pilot program well underway next year." Marles said.

Minister Kapavore said implementing the Pukpuk Treaty is one of my highest priorities.

“I look forward to working with Deputy Prime Minister Marles and our nations’ officials to finalise the priority arrangements and practical outcomes.

“The recruitment of Papua New Guineans to the ADF is momentous and will further strengthen our enduring bond. I’m pleased to say that Deputy Prime Minister Marles and I believe we can deliver the first pilot program in 2027.” Minister Kapavore said.

Australia and PNG continue to demonstrate the strength of the defence partnership between the two nations through recent cooperation activities such as Exercise Puk Puk 2026, which brings together military engineers from the PNG Defence Force (PNGDF) and ADF to deliver infrastructure upgrades at Igam Barracks in Lae; a PNGDF-led mission to transport essential health supplies to communities in West Sepik; hydrographic survey operations conducted by HMAS Leeuwin in partnership with the PNGDF Maritime Element; and the participation of two PNGDF aircraft in last month’s Exercise Pitch Black 2026.

item.title: Ahi woman heads overseas for new opportunity
item.description: Neralyn Lalo from Yalu village in Lae is the only Ahi woman selected under the Lae Labour Mobility Program. Lalo has taken part in the program since 2004. She says the opportunity will help her gain new skills, work experience and support a better future for her family.
item.content:encoded:
Neralyn Lalo from Yalu village in Lae is the only Ahi woman selected under the Lae Labour Mobility Program.

Lalo has taken part in the program since 2004. She says the opportunity will help her gain new skills, work experience and support a better future for her family.

“It gives me a chance to grow, learn new skills, gain new experience, meet new people and work towards my goal,” she said.

Lalo is encouraging other Ahi women and girls to take up similar opportunities.

She says women need to step outside their comfort zones and be willing to try.“If I can do it, I know you can make it,” she said.

Lalo hopes her journey will encourage more Ahi women to seek employment and training opportunities.

For her, the overseas job is a chance to learn, grow and build a better future.

item.title: POM under water rationing as major pipeline undergoes critical repairs
item.description: Residents and businesses across Port Moresby will face scheduled water shutdowns and phased rationing starting Friday evening, August 14, to Sunday, August 16, 2026. The temporary disruption will allow Water PNG to execute emergency repairs on a leaking section of a 65-year-old pipeline supplying water from the Rouna system.
item.content:encoded:
Residents and businesses across Port Moresby will face scheduled water shutdowns and phased rationing starting Friday evening, August 14, to Sunday, August 16, 2026.

The temporary disruption will allow Water PNG to execute emergency repairs on a leaking section of a 65-year-old pipeline supplying water from the Rouna system.

The aging pipeline, originally laid in the 1960s, is in a fragile state and past its structural lifespan.

Water PNG chief executive officer James Young said an international engineering effort involving specialists from Papua New Guinea, Australia, New Zealand, Asia, and Europe was activated when the leak was first identified to mitigate the risk of a complete system collapse.

"This collective effort has placed us in a more capable position with reduced risk of further bursts, and to have a shorter partial shutdown period than initially projected," Young said.

Local landowners from the Behori Clan have been engaged throughout the preparatory phase and will work at the site over the weekend to clear access roads, construct drainage channels, and assist technical teams .

"Across the Government, the deteriorated state of this essential water infrastructure is recognized, and it is accepted that there is no other option but to replace the pipeline," Young added. "We cannot keep interrupting water supply to the city every few months for repairs; we must install a new pipeline that will serve NCD and Central Province for decades to come."

To maintain partial supply during the repair window, Water PNG has grouped the city into four supply zones :

Water PNG has urged consumers to run taps for at least five minutes to flush out any sediment or boil water prior to consumption once full service is restored to their areas.

For additional inquiries during the repair period, members of the public can contact the Water PNG toll-free hotline on 1801013 or email hotline@waterpng.com.pg .
